newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank chief sees lower interbank rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank chief sees lower interbank rates.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Friday he expected Thai interbank rates to decline gradually after the U.S. dollar stabilised.
Rerngchai conceded that high Thai interbank rates in the past several months have partly contributed to the bearish performance of the Thai stock market which this week declined to a 51-month low.
"The stock market decline was partly due to interest rates and partly because of short-selling," he said.
Rerngchai's statement was in response to comments by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Friday that high interbank rates had hurt Thai stocks.
The minister said the overnight rate should ease to a proper level of about 10 percent from 12 percent quoted on Friday. The overnight rate averaged 12-13 percent in December.
Rerngchai told reporters the Bank of Thailand has the responsibility of stabilising the Thai money market and baht exchange rate.
He said on Thursday that liquidity in the local money market should not be allowed to rise too high or it may encourage speculation on a bullish dollar.

Rerngchai said on Friday a state-run fund for rehabilitating financial institutions was prepared to ease short-term liquidity problems faced by small finance companies that are not affiliated with banks and have small credit lines.

Many finance firms that also operate stockbroking businesses have been hurt by the Thai bourse's prolonged fall. The composite SET Index has lost about 16 percent since December 1. -- Bangkok newsroom (662)-2529950-3
